applicant_utility.summary: This is not a tuition scholarship: it is a free one-year DataCamp licence plus a four-session course, awarded to a small cohort each year with no money changing hands. Eligibility turns on demonstrated economic need and a social-media condition - you must like the official post and follow El Quantificador on at least one network. Once selected you agree to monthly checks in which LIDE inspects your DataCamp XP between the 3rd and 5th of each month, so the award only pays off if you can genuinely sustain a study habit for twelve months.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Low-income students or workers in Ecuador who want Excel, Power BI, Tableau, Python, R or SQL skills without paying for a platform and can protect a few study hours every week.
application_readiness_checklist: Set up or refresh an El Quantificador account on Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, Bluesky or Threads and keep both the like and the follow live until after the closing date
Use an email address you check every day - winners are contacted by email before 28 October 2026, not through a portal
Block the four course sessions (28-29 October and 4-5 November 2026) in your calendar before you apply, since the licence is scheduled to start 1 November 2026
Decide now which DataCamp track you will follow (Excel, Power BI, Tableau, R, Python or SQL) so your first weeks of activity are not wasted choosing
Submit the form early in the 18 September - 20 October 2026 window; nothing needs uploading, but a last-minute submission on the closing day leaves no room for a form error
common_rejection_risks: Dropping the social-media like or follow during the waiting period, when the call treats it as a condition of entry
Weak or vague answers to the form's economic-need and motivation questions - with no CV or transcript requested, the written answers carry all the weight
Losing the licence through inactivity: LIDE reviews XP monthly, and in the 2023-2024 round scholarships were withdrawn when there was no activity in the first two weeks
Missing the single email notification, which is the only channel used to reach winners in the week after closing
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Reliable internet access and a device that can run DataCamp, plus any transport or connectivity needed for the four-session course; LIDE funds no tuition, living stipend or travel of any kind.
document_audit: No CV, transcript, essay, certificate or reference letter is requested - the Google Form is your entire file
The form marks the email question as mandatory, and it warns you never to submit passwords through Google Forms
The form asks for consent to use your answers anonymously for research purposes; declining that voluntary question blocks submission
There is no document upload, so income evidence is conveyed in your own words rather than through proof
alerts: The call closes hard on 20 October 2026 and no extension or late route is published
The licence start of 1 November 2026 is not guaranteed - LIDE states it depends on DataCamp renewing and activating the licences and that it will inform fellows of operational delays
The Spanish call says no nationality or residence restriction while the form frames the audience as tertiary students in Ecuador, so be ready to explain a non-Ecuadorian application if you submit one
Monthly monitoring between the 3rd and 5th means a busy work or exam month can put continued access at risk
Former LIDE-DataCamp holders are explicitly allowed to reapply, so a previous rejection is not a bar
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the single Google Form linked in the official post, then wait for the selection email sent between 21 and 28 October 2026; selected fellows attend the course and receive the licence on 1 November 2026.
